items.title: Pilot: Region 2 "Two at once" as a puzzle ambush (Lichess puzzles instead of a custom battle)
items.body:
Pilot one Region 2 map node, **Two at once** (slot 3, double check), as an **ambush**: a short run of published Lichess puzzles framed as one fight. No engine plays and nothing needs `npm run verify:battles`. If the pilot works, most later map nodes become ambushes, and custom battles become occasional.

Region 1 keeps its built battles. Nothing in #24 is rewritten.

## Why

Custom battles are the slow part of building a Region. Each one is a position we invent, then playtest with simulated players: 24 games per player type and difficulty, re-run after every change (`scripts/verify/battles.verify.test.ts`). Lichess puzzles already carry a checked solution, a rating and themes, backed by engine analysis and many player attempts. That assurance holds only if we use the puzzle as published: the same position, the same solution line, the same replies. An ambush uses them that way.

Proposed long-term mix (to decide after the pilot, row D9 below):

| Content | Source and behaviour | Checking needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Most map nodes: **ambushes** | A short run of curated Lichess puzzles, with story, faction art and rewards | Solution replays, completion and reward tests, teaching review |
| Technique nodes | Cleared Lichess Practice chapters (opposition, rook mates, Lucena, Philidor) | Accepted answers and goals; engine checks only where play is open-ended |
| An occasional custom battle | Siege, escort or strategy scenario | Today's battle verification |
| Region boss | Live game with your army | Today's army and engine verification |

## Read first

- [Guided path](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/campaign.md#guided-path) and #24 (Region 1's revision to it).
- [Region 2 brief](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/regions/region-02-bandit-riders.md): slot 3 and the [wanted poster](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/regions/region-02-bandit-riders.md#ai-habit-wanted-poster).
- The bounty code this builds on: `src/game/bounty.ts` (`Puzzle`, `puzzleStart`, `checkPuzzleMove`) and `src/scenes/Puzzle.ts`.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/AGENTS.md): `src/game` has no screen code, every rule gets a test, and the Phaser pitfalls.

## Decisions to approve before code

The owner approves these rows in this issue, with edits if needed. The pilot PR then adds them to the [decision log](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/decisions.md). Numbers marked "first guess" also go in [Tuning values](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/systems.md#tuning-values) and the open questions.

| # | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| D1 | Region 2's **Two at once** (slot 3, double check) is built as an ambush to pilot puzzle-based map nodes. Region 1 keeps its built battles. More ambushes wait for the pilot's result (D9) |
| D2 | An **ambush** is a run of published Lichess puzzles framed as one fight. The enemy plays only the published replies, and the player never plays on past a puzzle's solution. This replaces the old ambush type ("a puzzle position, then play it out"). No engine plays in an ambush |
| D3 | Ambush difficulty changes the help, never the chess. Every difficulty plays the same puzzles in the pilot. Harder puzzle choices for Champion and Grandmaster come later, as different published puzzles, never different replies to the same puzzle |
| D4 | A wrong move in an ambush is taken back and counts as a miss; you try that position again. Miss limits (first guess): Gentle none, Brave 3, Champion and Grandmaster 2 in the whole ambush. Reaching the limit loses it, with the usual [loss cost](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/campaign.md#campaign-and-gauntlet), Grandmaster removal included (as decided in #24). Rewinds don't apply |
| D5 | A move is accepted when it's the published move, or when the published move mates and yours mates too (Lichess's own rule, already in `checkPuzzleMove`). No engine check: Lichess keeps only puzzles where each solver move is the one clearly winning move |
| D6 | Faction habits in an ambush may only **tell**. The wanted poster marks the piece that the published setup move (the puzzle's first move) captures or newly attacks, using the target rule from #12. There's no tilt, because the replies are fixed |
| D7 | An ambush pays its reward (15–25g) on the first win, plus two 5g bonus goals: **clean** (no misses) and **no hints**. It pays no tactic gold. On a solve, the banner names the puzzle's theme (DOUBLE CHECK!) without an engine check, because the tag comes from Lichess |
| D8 | The playbook's battle content rules (4–10 pieces a side, not winnable on the first move, a 5–10 move limit, one scripted line) and verification bars (90% strong, 40% careless, 4–7 moves) apply to custom battles and bosses only. Ambushes follow new ambush content rules instead (below) |
| D9 | After the pilot, the owner decides whether most map nodes become ambushes, using the pilot report (below). Lichess Practice technique nodes are decided then too |

## How an ambush plays

1. **Briefing** as for battles (`briefBattle` in `src/flow.ts`): story lines, the goal ("Break all 4 waves of the ambush"), both bonus goals, the reward and the miss limit for your difficulty.
2. **Show one.** Your companion plays through one double-check position and names the idea in a sentence or two, as a warm-up does. Skippable. An ambush has no separate warm-up: this is its teaching step, and the first wave is the test.
3. **Four waves.** Each wave is one puzzle, at rising ratings. The board shows the puzzle's setup move, then you solve. The enemy's replies inside a puzzle are the published ones, played with the usual animation.
4. **Help by difficulty:**

   | | Gentle | Brave | Champion | Grandmaster |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Companion line before each wave | Yes | First wave only | No | No |
   | Hint button (lights up the piece that moves) | Always | Always | No | No |
   | Misses before you lose | No limit | 3 | 2 | 2 |
   | Wanted poster | Yes, and the companion names the target | Yes | Yes | Yes |

   The hint uses the board's existing hint highlight on the piece only (from-square), not the move. Any hint costs the **no hints** bonus.
5. **Win:** all four waves solved. Pay the reward and bonuses through the same once-only paths as battles (`recordWin` in `src/game/economy.ts`, extended for the new bonus kinds).
6. **Loss:** the miss limit is reached. Record it as a battle loss (`recordLoss`). **Retry** restarts at wave 1 and uses the **backup** puzzle for the wave you lost on.
7. **Replay** of a cleared ambush, for its bonus goals, skips the show-one step and uses the main puzzles.
8. Leaving mid-ambush asks for confirmation and counts as a loss, as leaving a battle does (`settleUnrecorded` in `src/scenes/Battle.ts`).

## Content: Two at once

| Part | Pick |
| --- | --- |
| Tag | `doubleCheck` (about 4.9k puzzles pass our quality filter in Region 2's range, per the [battle outline](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/campaign.md#battle-outline-by-region)) |
| Show one | 1 puzzle, rated 600–800 |
| Waves 1–4 | Rated about 700, 850, 1000 and 1150 (±75), each with 1 backup in the same range |
| Total | 9 published puzzles, given by Lichess id |
| Reward | 20g, with **clean** and **no hints** at 5g each |
| Words | Briefing lines, the show-one line per starter (Sir Hob, Sage Ollie, Old Brick), one companion line per wave, 1–2 lines after a win, in the [voice guide](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/story.md#voice-and-dialogue). Our own words |

**Ambush content rules** (new playbook section, from D8):

- Every puzzle passes the bounty quality filter (`QUALITY` in `scripts/build-puzzles.mjs`) and carries the ambush's tag.
- The tagged idea is in the solution the player plays, not only in the setup move. For double check, a solver move gives double check. A content test checks this.
- 1–3 solver moves per puzzle.
- Ratings rise across the waves. The backup is within 75 points of its wave.
- No puzzle repeats inside an ambush, and none is a bounty or warm-up anywhere in the game.
- Pick each one by hand on the board. Prefer variety in the checking pieces (not four knight-and-rook double checks), and avoid puzzles where an untaught tactic carries the solution.
- Record each puzzle's id, its link (`https://lichess.org/training/<id>`) and why it was picked.
- The puzzle positions are used as published, so piece counts, first-move wins and move counts don't apply.

**Finding candidates.** The puzzle download (`npm run puzzles`) goes to `data/raw/`, which is never committed. Add a candidates mode to `scripts/build-puzzles.mjs`, for example `npm run puzzles -- --candidates doubleCheck --min 600 --max 1250`. It writes a short list (id, rating, solver moves, the checking pieces, link) to `data/raw/`, to pick from on lichess.org. Track the time picking takes; the pilot report needs it.

## Code

Suggested shape. Change it if the code argues otherwise, and say why in the PR.

- **`src/game/ambush.ts`** (no screen code): the `AmbushDef` type and the run rules as a small state machine.
  - `AmbushDef`: `id`, `kind: 'ambush'`, `title`, `theme`, `tag`, `reward`, `bonuses`, `before`, `after`, `tip`, `show` (one puzzle), `waves` (`{ main: Puzzle; backup: Puzzle }[]`), `faction`. Puzzles are inline, as warm-up puzzles are in #24's T2, so nothing is fetched at play time.
  - `AmbushRun`: current wave, solver step, misses, hints used, and which waves use their backup. Pure functions: `start(def, difficulty, { retryFromWave? })`, `move(run, uci)`, `hint(run)`, giving `correct`, `solved wave`, `miss`, `won` or `lost`. It reuses `puzzleStart` and `checkPuzzleMove`.
  - Miss limits and hint rules come from one table keyed by difficulty, so the numbers live in one place.
- **Bonus kinds:** add `clean` and `noHint` to `Bonus` in `src/game/content.ts`, with `bonusMet` and `bonusText`. Ambush stats are `{ won, misses, hintsUsed }`; keep the battle stats type unchanged.
- **Wanted poster target:** a pure function from a position and a move to the target square, following the target rule in the brief. If #12 has landed, reuse its function; if not, write it in `src/game/poster.ts` so #12 can reuse it.
- **Theme text:** add `doubleCheck` to `THEME_TEXT` (or reuse #24 T6a's version, which adds the new tags).
- **Scene:** an `ambush` scene. Use `src/scenes/Puzzle.ts` as the model: the board, flipping when the solver is Black, the setup-move animation, the session check after every `await`. Your side uses ally tokens with named characters from `assignCharacters(fen, roster, solver)` in `src/game/campaign.ts`. The enemy uses Bandit Rider art if #10 has landed, otherwise Region 1's. Use `goTo()` to change screens.
- **Shared with #24 T3 (#29).** T3's warm-up flow is also a run of puzzles with a hint. Whichever lands second should reuse the other's state machine rather than build a second one.
- **Getting there:** Region 2's map waits for the Region registry (#9). Until then, open the pilot from a dev-only URL, `?ambush=r2-two-at-once`, read in `src/main.ts` like `?loop=timeout`. Use a fresh test save on Brave, or the current save's difficulty if one exists. Not shown to players and not deployed as a map node. When #9 and #14 land, the map node points at the `AmbushDef` instead of a `BattleDef`.

## Tests

`npm run ci` before the PR. The ambush imports no AI or engine code, so `npm run ci -- --plan` should show no engine playtests. If it shows some, find the import that pulls them in.

- **Content** (`src/game/ambush.test.ts` or a Region 2 content test):
  - every puzzle replays legally from its FEN;
  - each carries `doubleCheck`, and a solver move really gives double check (`chess.attackers` on the king after the move finds two pieces);
  - 1–3 solver moves each, ratings rising across the waves, each backup within 75 of its wave;
  - ids unique inside the ambush, and not in any bounty pack (`public/puzzles/`) or warm-up.
- **Run rules:**
  - correct moves advance, and the published replies play;
  - a miss is counted and the position is offered again;
  - the miss limits per difficulty lose at the right count, and Gentle never loses;
  - an alternative mate is accepted, and any other move is a miss;
  - hints are counted, and none are available on Champion and Grandmaster;
  - a retry after a loss uses the backup for the lost wave only.
- **Economy:** the reward pays once; each bonus pays once; a loss costs gold per difficulty; a Grandmaster loss marks the node gone.
- **Poster:** the target rule on a capture, a new attack, a fork (highest value, then square order) and a quiet move (no poster).
- **Browser check** at the four playbook sizes (1280×800, 375×812, 375×553, 844×390): solve, miss, hint, lose, retry and win, with no console errors.

## Out of scope

- The Region 2 map, registry and other slots (#9, #11, #14). #11 should not design a custom position for slot 3 while this pilot runs.
- Region 1. Its battles and #24 go ahead unchanged.
- Harder puzzle choices for Champion and Grandmaster, and the adaptive rating.
- Lichess Practice technique nodes.
- Boss changes, and the wanted poster's tilt for live battles (#12).
- New art beyond a placeholder poster icon.

## Pilot report and go/no-go

Add a short report to [build progress](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/progress.md), and a summary comment here:

- **Authoring time:** picking puzzles, writing words, code for the content (not the shared code), compared with the owner's estimate for one Region 1 battle.
- **Yield:** candidates looked at before finding 9 good puzzles.
- **Play time:** minutes to finish, per difficulty. The target is 3–5 minutes, about a battle's length.
- **Feel:** at least 3 playtesters, on Gentle and Brave, answer one question: did it feel like a battle, or like bounties with a story around them? Note what they said about the poster and the show-one step.
- **Problems:** any rule above that didn't work in practice.

The owner then decides D9.

## Done when

- The decision rows are approved here and added to the decision log, with first-guess numbers in Tuning values and the open questions.
- The playbook has an **Ambush content rules** section, and its battle content rules and bars say they apply to custom battles and bosses (D8). `docs/design/systems.md` describes the ambush under battle types; Names and terms gets **Ambush**.
- The pilot plays from `?ambush=r2-two-at-once`, with all tests above passing and `npm run ci` green.
- The pilot report is written.

Related: #24 (guided path; T3 #29 shares the puzzle-run code), #8 and #11 (Region 2 spec and design), #12 (wanted poster), #9 (Region registry), #10 (art).

items.title: Region 2 detailed design: map, battles, warm-ups and dialogue
items.body:
Part of #8. Docs only, so it can start now, in parallel with the Region 1 guided path (#24) and the code groundwork.

Fill in the **To design** sections of the [Region 2 brief](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/regions/region-02-bandit-riders.md): the map, the battles, the warm-ups and the story lines. Then get the owner's approval before any content is built.

## Scope

- **The map:** a [guided path](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/campaign.md#guided-path) following the [map rules](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/playbook.md#map-rules). Slots 1–3 are the main path, in order (first ambush, double trouble, two at once). Slots 4 and 5 are branches (the banner wagons, into the trap). The boss opens after 4 wins.
- **Five battles** in the [slots in the brief](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/regions/region-02-bandit-riders.md#battles), each meeting the [content rules](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/playbook.md#battle-content-rules): positions as FEN, the goal, the idea, the scripted winning line and squad names.
  - The banner-wagon siege uses the raider after #23, and is designed so that taking a raider's defender is the way to win a trade.
- **Warm-ups:** one per battle, following the [warm-up rules](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/playbook.md#warm-up-content-rules), with the ideas and tags from the [battle outline](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/campaign.md#battle-outline-by-region): knight forks, double attacks, double check, taking the guard first, and mate in two.
  - Positions are published Lichess puzzles in the 600–1000 band, given by puzzle id.
  - Plus Ashfang's boss warm-up, on stopping a fork before it lands (`fork` with `defensiveMove`).
  - Use the warm-up table in the [Region template](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/regions/region-template.md).
- **Bounty tags:** `fork`, `doubleCheck`, `capturingDefender` and `mateIn2`, plus one or two from Region 1. Region 2 has no tip cards.
- **Dialogue:**
  - arrival;
  - each battle's lines before and after, its tip, and its one-line reminder;
  - each warm-up's shown text and hint;
  - the boss scene, Tadwell's lines and the Lich King's interlude.

  All of it per the [voice guide](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/story.md#voice-and-dialogue). Your starter companion coaches every warm-up. A line or two can call back to a Region 1 warm-up ("Remember the back rank?").
- **The boss army's exact pieces:** about 17 points, knight-heavy.
- **Every enemy habit** (wanted poster, raider) follows [tell or tilt, never force](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/systems.md#ai-habits-by-faction).
- **New names** go in [Names and terms](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/glossary.md) and the cast.

## Order

The design can be written now. It's easier to finalise after the Region 1 warm-ups (#24, T2) exist as a worked example, so expect a light pass once those land.

## Done when

The Region 2 document has no **To design** sections left (Verification and Playtest excepted), and the owner has approved it in this issue.

items.title: ACI 318-19 shear & P-M checks (rc_check / certify_rc_members) ignore axial tension on Vc, omit 420 MPa fyt and 8.3 MPa sqrt(f'c) caps, and mis-account displaced concrete in P-M interaction (overstating capacity by >37% and issuing false certified_ok)
items.body:
# Unconservative ACI 318-19 Shear & P–M Interaction Checks in `rc_check` and `certify_rc_members`

Bounty submission for #505.

## Metadata
- **Target Repository**: `lambdaclass/stabileo` (`engine/`)
- **Severity**: **Critical** (per `docs/SAFETY_ADVISORIES.md`: *"Unconservative by more than 10 % in a governing quantity, in a default workflow or a common model, with no warning"* and *"A check returns `pass` (`ratio ≤ 1.0`) or `certified_ok = true` on a member that should fail by more than 10%"*)
- **Affected Files & Symbols**:
  1. `engine/src/postprocess/rc_check.rs`:
     - `shear_capacity` (lines 400–449)
     - `check_single_rc_member` (line 197)
     - `interaction_point` (lines 322–347)
  2. `engine/src/certify/design.rs`:
     - `rc_ratio_enclosures` (line 899)
     - `interaction_moment_enclosure` (lines 821–861)
     - `certify_rc_members` (lines 923–931; exported to WASM at `engine/src/lib.rs`)

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Both the ACI 318-19 design checker (`check_rc_members`) and its interval-certified counterpart (`certify_rc_members`) share generic routines in `engine/src/postprocess/rc_check.rs` that contain four compounding unconservative defects:

1. **Axial Tension (`f.nu > 0`) Is Completely Ignored in Concrete Shear Capacity `Vc` (ACI 318-19 Table 22.5.5.1 & §22.5.5.1.1):**
   `RCDesignForces` provides `nu: Option<f64>` (tension-positive), and `check_single_rc_member` / `rc_ratio_enclosures` use `nu` for flexure and axial checks, **but `shear_capacity<T: Real>(m: &RCMemberData) -> T` does not accept `nu` at all**. Under ACI 318-19 Table 22.5.5.1 and §22.5.5.1.1, axial force modifies $V_c$ by $+N_{u,\text{ACI}} / (6 A_g) \cdot b_w d$ (where $N_{u,\text{ACI}} = -\text{nu}$ is negative in tension), reducing $V_c$ down to $0$ when tensile stress $\text{nu} / A_g \ge 6 \times 0.17\lambda\sqrt{f'_c} = 1.02\lambda\sqrt{f'_c}$ (and capping $N_{u,\text{ACI}} / (6 A_g) \le 0.05 f'_c$ and $V_c \le 0.42\lambda\sqrt{f'_c} b_w d$ in compression per §22.5.5.1.2). Unlike `cirsoc201_check.rs` (lines 486–499) and `ec2_check.rs` (lines 236–251), `rc_check.rs` credits **100% of the uncracked concrete shear capacity** $V_c$ even when the section is in full axial tension.

2. **Missing `fyt <= 420 MPa` Cap on Stirrup Yield Strength in `Vs` (ACI 318-19 Table 20.2.2.4(a) & §22.5.3.3):**
   Line 410 computes `vs = (T::exact(av) * T::exact(m.fy) * T::exact(m.d)).dv(T::exact(s))` using `m.fy` uncapped. Per ACI 318-19 Table 20.2.2.4(a) and §22.5.3.3, the value of $f_{yt}$ used to calculate $V_s$ shall not exceed $420\text{ MPa}$. (This cap was implemented in `cirsoc201_check.rs:467` per `docs/verification/TS_ENGINE_LOGIC.md` line 161, but left unfixed in `rc_check.rs`.) For $500\text{ MPa}$ or Grade 80 ($550\text{ MPa}$) reinforcement, `rc_check.rs` overstates $V_s$ by **+19.0%** and **+31.0%**, respectively.

3. **Missing `sqrt(f'c) <= 8.3 MPa` Cap on `vc_with_min`, `av_min_mm2`, and `vs_max` (ACI 318-19 §22.5.3.1):**
   Line 405 computes `let sqrt_fc = fc_mpa.sqrt();` uncapped and only applies `.min(T::lit(8.3))` inside `vc_without_min` (line 429). It leaves `vc_with_min` (line 415), `av_min_mm2` (line 435), and `vs_max = 0.66 * sqrt_fc * bw_mm * d_mm` (line 445) uncapped for $f'_c > 69\text{ MPa}$, violating ACI 318-19 §22.5.3.1 (which caps $\sqrt{f'_c} \le 8.3\text{ MPa}$ on $V_{s,\max}$ unconditionally and on $V_c$ unless special §22.5.3.2 beam/joist web reinforcement is provided).

4. **Displaced Concrete Mis-Accounting in P–M Interaction (`interaction_point`, lines 335–343):**
   - For the compression steel layer at $d'$, line 336 unconditionally subtracts displaced concrete: `let cs = as_comp * (fs_comp - T::lit(0.85) * fc);` even when $c < d'$ ($\varepsilon'_s < 0$, i.e. top steel is in the **tension zone** and displaces no compressed concrete; contrast `rc_flexure.rs:80` which branches on `zero.le(eps_sc)`).
   - Conversely, for the tension steel layer at $d$, line 341 computes `let t = T::exact(m.as_tension) * fs_tens;` **without** deducting displaced concrete $0.85 f'_c A_s$ when $c > d$ ($\varepsilon_t < 0$, bottom steel in compression under high axial load; contrast `cirsoc201_check.rs:375`). As a result, at large neutral axis depths $c > d$, $\phi P_n(c)$ in `interaction_point` exceeds the theoretical squash load $\phi P_o = 0.65 [0.85 f'_c (A_g - A_{st}) + f_y A_{st}]$.

---

## 2. Vulnerable Code

In `engine/src/postprocess/rc_check.rs`:

```rust
// Line 197: f.nu is never passed to shear_capacity
let phi_vn: f64 = shear_capacity(m);
```

```rust
// Lines 334-343:
// Compression steel: net of the concrete it displaces (even when c < d' and steel is in tension!)
let fs_comp = (strain_at(d_prime) * es).max(-fy).min(fy);
let cs = as_comp * (fs_comp - T::lit(0.85) * fc);

// Tension steel: positive strain_at means compression, so flip (never deducts 0.85*fc when c > d!)
let epsilon_t = -strain_at(d);
let fs_tens = (epsilon_t * es).max(-fy).min(fy);
let t = T::exact(m.as_tension) * fs_tens;
```

```rust
// Lines 400-449:
pub(crate) fn shear_capacity<T: Real>(m: &RCMemberData) -> T {
    let lambda = T::exact(m.lambda.unwrap_or(1.0));
    let fc_mpa = T::exact(m.fc).dv(T::exact(1e6));
    let bw_mm = T::exact(m.b) * T::exact(1000.0);
    let d_mm = T::exact(m.d) * T::exact(1000.0);
    let sqrt_fc = fc_mpa.sqrt(); // <-- Uncapped above 8.3 MPa
    let zero = T::exact(0.0);

    // Vs = Av * fy * d / s  <-- m.fy uncapped above 420 MPa (ACI 318-19 20.2.2.4 / 22.5.3.3)
    let vs = match (m.av, m.s_stirrup) {
        (Some(av), Some(s)) if s > 0.0 => (T::exact(av) * T::exact(m.fy) * T::exact(m.d)).dv(T::exact(s)),
        _ => zero,
    };

    // ACI 318-19 9.6.3.4: Av,min = max(0.062*sqrt(f'c)*bw*s/fyt, 0.35*bw*s/fyt)
    let vc_with_min = || T::lit(0.17) * lambda * sqrt_fc * bw_mm * d_mm; // <-- Ignores Nu/(6*Ag) and 8.3 MPa cap!
    // ...
    // Maximum Vs limit: 0.66 * sqrt(f'c_MPa) * bw_mm * d_mm (N)
    let vs_max = T::lit(0.66) * sqrt_fc * bw_mm * d_mm; // <-- Missing 8.3 MPa cap on sqrt_fc!
    let vs = vs.min(vs_max);

    T::lit(PHI_V) * (vc + vs)
}
```

And in `engine/src/certify/design.rs`:
```rust
// Line 899:
let phi_vn: Interval = rc_shear_capacity(m);
let shear = loaded_ratio(RC_CHECK_NAMES[1], vu, phi_vn)?;
```

---

## 3. Proof of Concept / Reproduction

### Case 1: RC Member Under Axial Tension + Shear (`check_rc_members` & `certify_rc_members`)
Consider a standard rectangular RC member ($b = 0.30\text{ m}$, $h = 0.50\text{ m}$, $d = 0.44\text{ m}$, $d' = 0.06\text{ m}$, $A_g = 0.15\text{ m}^2$, $f'_c = 28\text{ MPa}$, $f_y = 500\text{ MPa}$, $A_s = A'_s = 1500\text{ mm}^2$, 2-leg $\varnothing 10$ stirrups $A_v = 157\text{ mm}^2$ at $s = 0.20\text{ m}$) subjected to:
- Factored axial tension `nu = 350_000.0` N ($350\text{ kN}$ tension, so $N_{u,\text{ACI}} = -350\text{ kN}$ and axial stress $N_{u,\text{ACI}} / A_g = -2.333\text{ MPa}$)
- Factored shear `vu = 200_000.0` N ($200\text{ kN}$)
- Factored moment `mu = 50_000.0` N·m ($50\text{ kN}\cdot\text{m}$)

**1. True ACI 318-19 Calculation:**
- By Table 22.5.5.1(a) and §22.5.5.1.1:

$$V_c = \max\left(0,\; \left(0.17\lambda\sqrt{f'_c} + \frac{N_{u,\text{ACI}}}{6 A_g}\right) b_w d\right) = (0.17\sqrt{28} - 0.3889)\times 300 \times 440 = 67.41\text{ kN}$$

- By Table 20.2.2.4(a) and §22.5.3.3 ($f_{yt} = \min(500, 420) = 420\text{ MPa}$):

$$V_s = \frac{157 \times 420 \times 440}{200} = 145.07\text{ kN}$$

- Design shear capacity:

$$\phi V_n = 0.75 (67.41 + 145.07) = 159.36\text{ kN}$$

- True shear utilization:

$$\frac{V_u}{\phi V_n} = \frac{200.0}{159.36} = 1.2550 > 1.0 \quad (\text{FAIL})$$

**2. Stabileo `check_rc_members` & `certify_rc_members` Output:**
- Ignores `nu` in $V_c$, computing $V_c = 0.17\sqrt{28}\times 300\times 440 = 118.74\text{ kN}$ (+76.1% too high).
- Uses uncapped $f_y = 500\text{ MPa}$ in $V_s$, computing $V_s = 172.70\text{ kN}$ (+19.0% too high).
- Reports $\phi V_n = 0.75(118.74 + 172.70) = 218.58\text{ kN}$ (**+37.2% unconservative overstatement**).
- Reports `shear_ratio = 0.9150 <= 1.0`, `unity_ratio = 0.9150 <= 1.0`, and `certify_rc_members` returns **`certified: true`, `certified_ok: true`, `certified_fail: false`**.
- *(Note: at higher axial tension `nu >= 810 kN` without stirrups, ACI 318-19 requires $V_c = 0$, whereas Stabileo reports $\phi V_n = 89.06\text{ kN}$ and `certified_ok: true` on a member with **zero** shear capacity.)*

---

## 4. Recommended Fix

1. Update `shear_capacity<T: Real>(m: &RCMemberData, axial_compression: T) -> T` to:
   - Cap `sqrt_fc = fc_mpa.sqrt().min(T::lit(8.3))` globally per ACI 318-19 §22.5.3.1 (as in `cirsoc201_check.rs:460`).
   - Cap `fyt_vs = m.fy.min(420e6)` in $V_s$ per ACI 318-19 §20.2.2.4 / §22.5.3.3 while keeping actual `m.fy` in $A_{v,\min}$ (as in `cirsoc201_check.rs:467–472`).
   - Include the axial stress term `axial = (axial_compression / (ag * 1e6) / 6.0).min(0.05 * fc_mpa)` in $V_c$, clamped to `[0.0, 0.42 * lambda * sqrt_fc * bw_mm * d_mm]` per ACI 318-19 Table 22.5.5.1, §22.5.5.1.1, and §22.5.5.1.2, and pass `-nu` from `check_single_rc_member` and `rc_ratio_enclosures`.
2. In `interaction_point`, only deduct displaced concrete $0.85 f'_c$ when a steel layer is in compression (`branch(zero.le(strain_at(d_prime)), ...)` for compression steel, and deduct `0.85 * fc` from the tension steel when `epsilon_t < 0`).

items.title: [Bug bounty] Native getTransferableAmount subtracts existential deposit twice

items.body:
# 🐞 Bug Report

## 🔍 Describe the Bug

For **native** assets, the existential deposit (ED) is subtracted twice when computing the transferable amount.

1. Native balances go through `SubstrateChain.getBalanceNative` → `SystemPallet.getBalance` ([SubstrateChain.ts:462–468, 509–511](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/sdk-core/src/chains/SubstrateChain.ts#L462-L511)). Since [#1903](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/pull/1903) (Jun 11), `SystemPallet.getBalance` returns the **spendable** balance, `free − max(frozen − reserved, ED)`, so the ED is already excluded ([SystemPallet.ts:32–41](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/sdk-core/src/pallets/system/SystemPallet.ts#L32-L41)).
2. `computeTransferableAmount` then subtracts the ED again ([getTransferableAmount.ts:68](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/transferable-amount/getTransferableAmount.ts#L68)):

```ts
const transferable = balance - BigInt(asset.existentialDeposit) - fee
```

Before #1903, `SystemPallet.getBalance` returned the raw `free` balance, so this single subtraction was correct. #1903 changed only `SystemPallet.ts` and its test, and the code that consumes that balance was not updated. The existing `getTransferableAmount` tests mock `getAssetBalanceInternal` with a raw balance, so they don't go through `SystemPallet` and couldn't catch it.

Foreign-asset pallets (`Assets`, `ForeignAssets`, `Tokens`, …) still return **raw** balances, so the ED subtraction is correct for them. Only native assets are affected.

**Why it matters:** For `amount: 'ALL'`, [normalizeAmountAll.ts:47–69](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/sdk-core/src/builder/normalizeAmountAll.ts#L47-L69) uses this result to build a cross-chain transaction. Under the same fee estimate, its resolved native-asset amount is one ED lower when the result stays positive. I have verified this calculation and build path, but have not signed or submitted a send-max transfer. Local native send-max uses `Balances.transfer_all`, whose call does not use this calculated amount. When `ED + fee < free ≤ 2 × ED + fee` (with no reserved or frozen funds), the SDK can return **0** despite a positive origin-side remainder.

## 🧪 To Reproduce

**Unit test** (save as `packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/transferable-amount/double-ed.repro.test.ts`). It mocks `getAssetBalanceInternal` to call the **real** `SystemPallet.getBalance`, which is the path native balances take:

```ts
import type { TAssetInfo } from '@paraspell/assets'
import { Version } from '@paraspell/sdk-common'
import { expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'

import type { PolkadotApi } from '../../api'
import { getAssetBalanceInternal } from '../../balance'
import { SystemPallet } from '../../pallets/system/SystemPallet'
import type { TGetTransferableAmountOptions, TXcmFeeDetail } from '../../types'
import { abstractDecimals } from '../../utils'
import { getOriginXcmFee } from '../fees'
import { getTransferableAmount } from './getTransferableAmount'

vi.mock('../../balance')
vi.mock('../../utils')
vi.mock('../fees')

it('reserves the native existential deposit only once', async () => {
  const asset = {
    symbol: 'DOT',
    decimals: 10,
    existentialDeposit: '100',
    location: { parents: 1, interior: { Here: null } }
  } as TAssetInfo
  const api = {
    queryState: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ data: { free: 1000n, reserved: 0n, frozen: 0n } }),
    findAssetInfoOrThrow: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(asset),
    findNativeAssetInfoOrThrow: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(asset),
    disconnect: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)
  } as unknown as PolkadotApi<unknown, unknown, unknown>

  vi.mocked(abstractDecimals).mockImplementation(amount => BigInt(amount))
  vi.mocked(getAssetBalanceInternal).mockImplementation(async () =>
    new SystemPallet('System').getBalance(api, 'validAddress', asset)
  )
  vi.mocked(getOriginXcmFee).mockResolvedValue({ fee: 200n, asset } as TXcmFeeDetail)

  const options = {
    api,
    sender: 'validAddress',
    origin: 'Polkadot',
    destination: 'AssetHubPolkadot',
    currency: { symbol: 'DOT', amount: 1000n },
    version: Version.V5,
    buildTx: vi.fn(async () => ({}))
  } as TGetTransferableAmountOptions<unknown, unknown, unknown>

  // Free 1000 minus ED 100 minus fee 200 should leave 700.
  await expect(getTransferableAmount(options)).resolves.toBe(700n)
})
```

```sh
pnpm --filter @paraspell/sdk-core exec vitest run src/transfer/transferable-amount/double-ed.repro.test.ts
```

It fails: received **600** instead of **700**.

**Supplementary live, read-only observation (Polkadot relay, October 21, 2026).** Using the built `@paraspell/sdk` 14.4.4 on a public account (`13UVJyLnbVp9RBZYFwFGyDvVd1y27Tt8tkntv6Q7JVPhFsTB`, no reserved or frozen balance). Nothing was signed or submitted. This snippet is abridged; imports and the `WHO` address declaration are omitted:

```js
const b = Builder().from('Polkadot').to('AssetHubPolkadot')
  .currency({ symbol: 'DOT', amount: 10_000_000_000n }).recipient(WHO).sender(WHO);
const spendable = await getBalance({ chain: 'Polkadot', address: WHO, currency: { symbol: 'DOT' } });
const { fee } = await b.getOriginXcmFee();
const transferable = await b.getTransferableAmount();
```

## 🖥️ Environment

- OS: Windows
- XCM Tool: XCM SDK (`@paraspell/sdk-core` / `@paraspell/sdk` 14.4.4, `main` at `de8d226`)
- Node.js: v24.20.0

## 📸 Screenshots / Logs

Unit test:

```text
× reserves the native existential deposit only once
- Expected: 700n
+ Received: 600n
Tests  1 failed (1)
```

Live read-only values, displayed to six decimal places:

```text
System.Account          : free ≈ 3117.894429 DOT; reserved = 0; frozen = 0
getBalance (spendable)  : ≈ 3116.894429 DOT
separate origin fee query: ≈ 0.057910 DOT
getTransferableAmount   : ≈ 3115.836518 DOT
```

The separate `b.getOriginXcmFee()` call uses the actual destination, while `getTransferableAmount()` estimates its fee with `destination: chain`. These displayed observations are consistent with the finding but do not prove an exact one-ED live difference. The controlled unit test above establishes the double subtraction.

## 💡 Expected Behavior

For a native asset, the transferable amount should be `spendable − fee`, with the ED reserved once. In the controlled test above, that is `1000 − 100 − 200 = 700`, rather than `600`.

Possible fix direction: skip the extra ED subtraction in `computeTransferableAmount` when the asset is the chain's native asset, since `SystemPallet.getBalance` has already excluded it. Keep it for foreign assets, whose pallets return raw balances. Simply deleting the subtraction is **not** correct because foreign assets still need it. The existing native-asset tests mock a raw balance, so they would need updating to match the spendable semantics.

## 📍 Additional Context

**Impact and limits:**

- The demonstrated path affects native assets with a nonzero ED on supported Substrate chains using `SystemPallet.getBalance`; no `getBalanceNative` override appears in current `main`. With enough balance, the reported maximum is one native ED too low.
- `getTransferableAmount()` under-reports the origin-side amount. The cross-chain `ALL` normalizer uses that reduced value to build a transaction, but I have not signed or submitted one. For `ED + fee < free ≤ 2 × ED + fee` with no reserved or frozen funds, the SDK returns zero despite a positive origin-side remainder; destination constraints were not tested.
- Related paths worth checking, but **not validated here**, are `@paraspell/swap`'s [getTransferableAmount](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/swap/src/transfer/getTransferableAmount.ts#L35-L52) and the SDK's [isSufficient checks](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/fees/isSufficient.ts#L31-L78).


**Duplicates:** I searched issues and PRs for transferable amount, existential deposit, SystemPallet, spendable balance, and max transferable. Nothing reports this; the related PRs (#1903, #2125, #2130) don't mention it.

items.body:
# 🐞 Bug Report

## 🔍 Describe the Bug

`calculateFee` passes the raw-unit `bigint` amount to `TradeRouter.getBestSell` **as a string** ([calculateFee.ts:27–31](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/swap/src/exchanges/Hydration/utils/calculateFee.ts#L27-L31)):

```ts
const trade = await tradeRouter.getBestSell(
  currencyFromInfo.id,
  currencyToInfo.id,
  amount.toString(), // raw units, e.g. "1000000000000" for 1 HDX
);
```

In `@galacticcouncil/sdk-next` 2.3.2, `TradeRouter.toSellSwaps` treats a string as a decimal token amount and scales it by the asset's decimals (a `bigint` is used as-is). So the fee-estimation trade is built for `amount × 10^decimals`. For example, 1000 HDX is quoted as 10¹⁵ HDX.

The real swap path handles this correctly. It calls `formatUnits(amountWithoutFee, decimals)` before `getBestSell` ([HydrationExchange.ts:69–78](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/swap/src/exchanges/Hydration/HydrationExchange.ts#L69-L78)), and `getAmountOut` does the same ([L162–168](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/de8d2266ced92c755655e861d17c7dddcc00a25a/packages/swap/src/exchanges/Hydration/HydrationExchange.ts#L162-L168)). As a result, the fee is estimated on a different (oversized) trade than the one that is actually submitted.

The read-only fee comparisons and their limits are under Additional Context. I have not measured a funded account's final fee, swap outcome, or balance change.

## 🧪 To Reproduce

**Unit test.** Add this inside the existing `describe('calculateFee', …)` in `packages/swap/src/exchanges/Hydration/utils/calculateFee.test.ts`. It uses the file's existing imports and `mockTxBuilderFactory`:

```ts
it('quotes the fee transaction with a human-readable token amount', async () => {
  const options = {
    amount: 1_000_000_000_000n, // 1 HDX (12 decimals)
    slippagePct: '1',
    feeCalcAddress: 'someAddress',
  } as TPapiSwapOptions<unknown, unknown, unknown>;
  const currencyFromInfo = { id: 0, symbol: 'HDX', decimals: 12 } as Asset;
  const currencyToInfo = { id: 2, symbol: 'DOT' } as Asset;
  const getBestSell = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ amountOut: 1000n });
  const tradeRouter = { getBestSell } as unknown as TradeRouter;

  await calculateFee(options, tradeRouter, mockTxBuilderFactory, currencyFromInfo, currencyToInfo, 12, 'Hydration', 2n);

  expect(getBestSell).toHaveBeenCalledWith(0, 2, '1');
});
```

```sh
pnpm --filter @paraspell/swap exec vitest run src/exchanges/Hydration/utils/calculateFee.test.ts
```

The new test fails (`"1000000000000"` received instead of `"1"`), and the 4 existing tests pass.

**Live, read-only check (optional).** I quoted each pair on Hydration mainnet twice: once the way `swapCurrency` does (decimal string) and once the way `calculateFee` does (raw units as a string). For each quote I built the tx with the SDK's `txBuilderFactory` and read `partial_fee` via `tx.getPaymentInfo(getFakeTxCreator(addr))`, the same call ParaSpell's `getPaymentInfo` uses. Nothing was signed or submitted. Core of the script:

```js
const sdk = await createSdkContext(createClient(getWsProvider('wss://hydration-rpc.n.dwellir.com')));
for (const arg of [formatted /* e.g. "100" */, raw.toString() /* e.g. "100000000" */]) {
  const trade = await sdk.api.router.getBestSell(from.id, to.id, arg);
  const tx = (await sdk.tx.trade(trade).withSlippage(1).withBeneficiary(ADDR).build()).get();
  const { partial_fee } = await tx.getPaymentInfo(getFakeTxCreator(ADDR));
}
```

I can share the full script on request.

## 🖥️ Environment

- OS: Windows
- XCM Tool: XCM Router / `@paraspell/swap` 14.4.3 (local commit `82266c9`). `calculateFee.ts` is unchanged on current `main` (`de8d226`).
- Node.js: v24.20.0
- Hydration router: `@galacticcouncil/sdk-next` 2.3.2, `polkadot-api` 3.2.2 (live check)

## 📸 Screenshots / Logs

Unit test:

```text
- Expected: getBestSell(0, 2, "1")
+ Received: getBestSell(0, 2, "1000000000000")
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

Live read-only check using an unfunded address, Hydration mainnet, October 21, 2026. The table shows `partial_fee` for constructed, unsigned transactions; “normal input” uses `swapCurrency`'s amount formatting, and “raw string” uses `calculateFee`'s input:

| Pair (amount) | Route: normal input → raw string | `partial_fee` normal input | `partial_fee` raw string | Diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HDX→USDT (1000) | same (3 hops) | 0.369518 HDX | 0.369518 HDX | 0% |
| DOT→HDX (10) | same (2 hops) | 0.346842 HDX | 0.346842 HDX | 0% |
| USDT→DOT (100) | 4 hops → 5 hops | 0.387178 HDX | 0.409854 HDX | **+5.9%** |
| HOLLAR→HDX (1 and 1000) | not recorded | 0.329182 HDX | 0.362224 HDX | **+10.0%** |
| 4-Pool, HUSDe, GETH → HDX (1 and 1000) | not recorded | equal | equal | 0% |

The oversized quotes also carry router errors (e.g. DOT→HDX: `TradeNotAllowed, MaxInRatioExceeded, MaxOutRatioExceeded`; HDX→USDT: `MaxInRatioExceeded`), but neither `calculateFee` nor the tx builder checks them.

## 💡 Expected Behavior

The fee should be estimated on the trade that will actually be submitted. Passing `formatUnits(amount, currencyFromDecimals)` matches `swapCurrency` and `getAmountOut`. With that one-line change (plus the `formatUnits` import from `@paraspell/sdk-core`), all 5 tests in the file pass. Passing the `bigint` directly would also work, because the router uses a `bigint` as raw units without scaling.

## 📍 Additional Context

**What the impact is, and isn't:**

- In 2 of 7 read-only comparisons using an unfunded address, the constructed transaction's `partial_fee` was **5.9% or 10.0% higher** (about 0.02–0.03 HDX). For USDT→DOT, the raw-string quote used 5 pools instead of 4. The other 5 pairs had the same `partial_fee`. These are transaction fee estimates, not measurements of the final fee deducted by `calculateFee`.
- When an `origin` is set, `swapCurrency` subtracts the calculated `tradeFee` from the swap amount (`amount - tradeFee`). The effect on a funded user's final swap and balance was not measured in this check.
- No read-only quote or transaction-building step failed in my tests, including 1000 units of 18-decimal assets, where the inflated amount exceeds the u128 range. That is because the estimate is built as `Router.sell_all`, which doesn't encode `amount_in`.
- **Limitation:** my test address had no balance, so both the real and the estimate trades were built as `Router.sell_all`. For a funded account, the real trade would normally be `Router.sell` / `Omnipool.sell`, while the estimate would still be `sell_all` (its inflated amount always exceeds the balance). I did not measure that case.

**Suggested severity: 🟢 Low.** The measured read-only `partial_fee` differences were small; I have not measured the final fee or swap outcome for a funded account. For comparison, [#1484](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/issues/1484) was closed as a marginal (~$0.01) fee difference. I'm reporting this one because it's a separate root cause (wrong units passed to the router), and because it can change which route the fee is estimated on.

**Duplicates:** I searched issues and PRs for `calculateFee` / Hydration fee. [#1484](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/issues/1484) and [#2049](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/issues/2049) concern the destination fee being added twice and the fee buffer multiplier, not the input units.

items.title: [Bug] cordis.patch.yml 把 timeoutMs 也调到 300000：PowerContext Server 挂起时每条用户消息在 agent/pre-step 被阻塞最长 300 s，与 README「fail-open，绝不阻塞」不符
items.body:
## 摘要

提交 46213c1（「raise plugin HTTP timeouts to 300s so GLM generation (~44s) no longer surfaces as unavailable」）把 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的 `timeoutMs` 和 `requestTimeoutMs` 都改成了 `300000`。`timeoutMs` 是 `agent/pre-step` 召回的总期限（`src/index.ts:87`：`AbortSignal.timeout(runtime.config.timeoutMs)`），召回在模型步之前同步等待。结果是：Server 接受连接但不回应（卡住、过载、`prepare_context` 内部模型很慢）时，每条用户消息要等满 300 s 才进入模型。代码默认值 `timeoutMs: 4000` / `requestTimeoutMs: 1000`（`src/config.ts:45-46`）下是 1.1 s 放行。

README 写的是「Server 不可用时 fail-open，绝不阻塞正常工作」。

## 环境

- commit `46213c1`（0.0.3），Linux aarch64，Node 22.23.3。
- 宿主 `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2`：`dsh plugin --profile web add link:<仓库>` 后，`dsh --profile web --dump-config` 显示插件层生效配置为 `timeoutMs: 300000`、`requestTimeoutMs: 300000`。
- Server 用 127.0.0.1 上的本地模拟代替，`/v1/context/prepare` 永不回应。

## 复现

`repro/pc/C1_hang_prestep.mjs`（真实 `apply()` + 插件注册的 `agent/pre-step` 处理器）：
```
[C1] 代码默认值（timeoutMs=4000）: 1.1 s 后放行（fail-open），决定=enter
[C1] cordis.patch.yml 发行值（timeoutMs=300000）: 60 s 后模型步仍未放行（settled=false）；改由用户手动取消
[C1] 缩比 timeoutMs=15000：3 轮各阻塞 15.0 / 15.0 / 15.0 s，累计 45.0 s（发行值下每轮上限 300 s）
```

## 建议

- pre-step 召回的总期限保持秒级（默认 4 s），300 s 只用于 `pc_experience_generate` / `pc_skill_generate` 等显式生成工具；
- 或在 patch 中只调高 `requestTimeoutMs`，pre-step 使用独立的、较短的 `recallTimeoutMs`；
- 召回超时被跳过时，可以在会话里留一条简短 notice，而不只写 warn 日志。

# dsh-review 问题汇总（0.3.0 @ `53a30cf`）

以下是本机实测看到的行为，每条附位置、判据与修复方向；对应测评报告：#1000（dsh-bounty）。涉及可直接利用载荷的条目按仓库 SECURITY.md 走私密通道，公开面只留判据。


---

## 1. [Bug][P1] 复核票的确定性校验不绑定候选：≥12 字符任意理由 + 任意快照行（含空行）即可清除真实缺陷 / 自动记 fixed

**触发条件**

verifier 输出 `{"decision":"reject","reason":"zzzzzzzzzzzz","witnesses":[{"file":"src/a.js","line":2,"anchor":""}]}`（第 2 行是空行，与候选所在第 3 行无关）。

**复现**

（步骤含可直接利用的细节，按仓库 `SECURITY.md` 私下提供；本条的判据、位置与读数见上。）

**预期**

README「复核必须说明具体成因并引用快照中的真实代码行。一个非空 evidence 字符串不算验证」「只有独立复核确认问题已消失，才能自动记为 fixed」；verifier 提示词「confirm requires evidence linked to this introducing change」。

**根因**

`src/gate.ts:47-49` 的 parseVote 只检查 reason.trim().length ≥ 12、每个 witness 能被 sourceMatches 命中；没有检查 witness 与 candidate 的文件/位置关系，也接受空锚点。`src/gate.ts:79` 在 reject 时直接把已发表问题记为 fixed（targetId 变化即可），不核对原锚点是否仍在。

**影响**

verifier 偷懒、幻觉或被被审代码中的文字诱导时，确定性层不会兜底：真实缺陷被一票（quick）清除且门禁放行；未修复的缺陷被自动记 fixed。真实模型下的发生率我们没有测（需付费 API）。

**建议**

① confirm/reject 至少一个 witness 落在 candidate 的文件且邻近 candidate 行（或 introducedBy 行）；② 拒绝空锚点 / 纯空白锚点 witness；③ reject 一个已发表问题记 fixed 前，确认原 anchor 在原位置已不存在（anchor 仍在则记 unverifiable 或 wrong 待人处理）。

**复现**

（步骤含可直接利用的细节，按仓库 `SECURITY.md` 私下提供；本条的判据、位置与读数见上。）

---

## 2. [Bug][P1] .dsh-review/ 与 @profile/ 目录下的改动在默认配置下不进审阅快照、不计入风险分级，门禁可直接放行

**触发条件**

默认 `stateDir: "@profile"`。PR 只新增 `.dsh-review/payments/charge.js` 与 `@profile/auth/login.js`。

**复现**

（步骤含可直接利用的细节，按仓库 `SECURITY.md` 私下提供；本条的判据、位置与读数见上。）

**预期**

README「跳过的路径会公开列出，并仍参与风险判断」。vendor/** 确实如此，这两个目录不是。

**根因**

`src/target.ts:59-60`：`internal` 在 stateDir 为 `@profile` 时等于字面量 `'@profile'`，且 `inState` 永远额外排除 `.dsh-review`；`src/target.ts:92` 的 `allPaths` 把 inState 路径去掉，classifyRisk 看不到。门禁输出（verdict）也不列出被排除路径。

**影响**

任何人都可以把代码放到这两个目录名下绕过 AI 审阅和敏感路径升级（再从被审文件里 import 一行即可执行）。

**建议**

只在 stateDir 实际解析到仓库内时排除那一个真实目录；`@profile` 模式下不排除任何仓库路径；被排除路径仍进入 allPaths/风险分级，并在 review_run / review_gate 结果里列出。

items.title: Fiddy: Farcaster client + read node + 3-command tutorial ($2048 bounty)
items.body:
# Fiddy — Farcaster Client + Read Node + 3-Command Tutorial (Bounty Spec)

## Problem Statement

Farcaster's documentation for standing up a read node and building a client is scattered across doc sites, some of it stale (it still describes onchain signer registration and claims read nodes reject writes). A developer who wants practical freedom of association — their own client on their own node, no third-party API keys — faces days of piecing together contracts, Snapchain, signers, and storage rent. Fiddy (fiddy.fun) wants to be the client that proves how easy this can be, and win the $2,048 bounty by getting it down to three commands.

## Solution

Ship three things as one coherent product:

1. **The Fiddy client** — a fork of `0xterricola/farcaster-wallet-client` (itself a fork of the Farcaster client snapshot with external wallet support), rebranded with the Fiddy identity (chartreuse / #161715, Solid Glass + Awwwards-grade UI), reading from the user's own Snapchain read node and writing through it (read nodes gossip valid messages to validators — no API keys, no Neynar, no Alchemy).
2. **One-click node deploy** — an agent-on-cloud service: the user furnishes compute (any VPS; AWS path scripted first, ~$100/mo), Fiddy provisions and boots a Snapchain read node, then points the client at it.
3. **The tutorial microsite** — quickstart at the top (three commands), then a mobile- and desktop-friendly tutorial that teaches protocol concepts as it goes: FIDs, custody addresses, app keys (gasless `KEY_ADD`), Snapchain messages, read nodes vs validators and the mempool path, storage rent, seed-phrase safety.
4. **The Fiddy Agent (the differentiator)** — every client user can hatch their own autonomous Hermes agent, hosted on Agent37 cloud, living inside the client. Not a chatbot bolt-on: a real Hermes instance with its full feature set — scheduled tasks (cron), skills, memory, and every messaging channel Hermes supports (Farcaster first, then iMessage, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, email, web/API) — with owner approval on every channel connection. No other Farcaster client ships an agent that works for you 24/7 across your whole communication surface.

Submission: reply to the bounty cast with (1) microsite URL, (2) github.com/ivcained/fiddy (MIT), (3) a voucher's public Farcaster endorsement. Deadline: 7 days from the bounty post (~2026-10-25).

## User Stories

### Quickstart & tutorial
1. As a developer, I want a quickstart at the very top of the page with exactly three commands, so that I know the whole shape of the task before reading anything.
2. As a developer, I want command (0) to provision compute via script, so that I don't click through a cloud console.
3. As a developer, I want command (1) to set up a Snapchain read node on that compute, so that it syncs the network with no API keys from anyone.
4. As a developer, I want command (2) to create a client that reads from my node, so that I see my own infra serving real Farcaster data.
5. As a developer, I want the tutorial to explain FIDs, custody addresses, app keys, Snapchain messages, read nodes vs validators, and storage rent inline as I encounter them, so that I learn the protocol instead of cargo-culting commands.
6. As a developer, I want the tutorial to explain that read nodes accept `submitMessage` and gossip to validators (no mempool of their own), and that a successful response means "accepted for relay, not in a block" — so that I confirm inclusion via `MERGE_MESSAGE` events or query-back instead of assuming.
7. As a developer, I want the tutorial to work on my phone and my desktop, so that I can follow along from either.
8. As a developer evaluating the tutorial, I want prominent seed-phrase safety guidance — use a test account only, never paste a seed into software from devs you don't trust, prefer delegated signer authorization — so that I don't burn a real account.
9. As a non-English speaker, I want at least a Chinese translation, so that I can follow the tutorial (extra-mile).
10. As a skimmer, I want a ~59s vertical video showing the three commands running, so that I believe it's real before investing an hour (extra-mile).

### Client
11. As a user, I want to import an existing seed phrase for an account that already has storage, so that I don't pay for a new FID.
12. As a user, I want the client to issue itself its own app key via gasless `KEY_ADD` (EIP-712 from my custody address, no Optimism transaction, no ETH), so that posting works in seconds.
13. As a user, I want to read my feed from my own read node, so that no third party mediates my reads.
14. As a user, I want to post casts, follow, and react, so that the client is genuinely usable.
15. As a user, I want to include/exclude casts from any other client, so that I control my experience.
16. As a user, I want external wallet support (WalletConnect EVM + Solana, EIP-6963 discovery, MetaMask Connect) — inherited from the upstream fork — so that I keep control of my keys.
17. As a user, I want the Fiddy brand (chartreuse on #161715, glass surfaces, award-level polish) so that the client feels like Fiddy, not a reskin of Warpcast.
18. As a user, I want one-click deploy of my own read node to cloud as a service, so that the client is self-sufficient without me babysitting a server.
19. As a user, I want the app-key scopes and 90-day sliding TTL explained at the moment I create one, so that I understand what the client can and cannot do in my name.
20. As a user, I want to revoke the client's app key (`KEY_REMOVE`) from the UI, so that I can cut access without onchain transactions.

### Fiddy Agent (Hermes on Agent37)
21. As a user, I want to hatch my own Fiddy agent from inside the client — one click provisions a dedicated Hermes instance on Agent37 cloud — so that I have an autonomous agent without touching a server.
22. As a user, I want to chat with my agent inside the client, so that it feels native, not like a separate app.
23. As a user, I want to schedule tasks for my agent (cron-style: "check my mentions every morning", "draft a weekly recap cast"), so that it works while I sleep.
24. As a user, I want to connect my agent to iMessage, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, email, and web/API — every channel Hermes supports — with an explicit approval step per channel, so that my agent meets people where they are and I stay in control.
25. As a user, I want my agent to act on Farcaster under its own identity (its own FID + gasless app key), so that its casts, replies, and follows are clearly the agent's, with me able to revoke its key at any time.
26. As a user, I want the agent's capabilities presented honestly as Hermes' full feature set — skills, memory, tools, scheduling — so that the offering is "a real Hermes instance that is yours," not a wrapped chatbot.
27. As a user, I want my agent to grow with me — persona drafted from my casts, memory persisted across sessions — so that it becomes more useful over time.
28. As the maintainer, I want the agent to dogfood the client's own read node, so that the agent proves the infra story end to end.

### Bounty operations
29. As the maintainer, I want the repo MIT-licensed with all code open, so that the entry qualifies.
30. As the maintainer, I want at least one human to complete the tutorial and publicly vouch on Farcaster, so that the entry qualifies — and more vouches as the strongest signal.
31. As the maintainer, I want stale upstream docs fixed via PRs to farcasterxyz repos when found (hand-written, not AI slop), so that the entry stands out and other devs benefit.
32. As the maintainer, I want fiddy.fun and the LC gateway VPS synced with the client work, so that the tutorial microsite and one-click deploy land on existing infra.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Repo**: `github.com/ivcained/fiddy`, forked from `0xterricola/farcaster-wallet-client` (done). MIT license retained. Upstream remote kept for snapshot review before merges.
- **Monorepo layout (inherited)**: `apps/farcaster-web` (Vite web client — primary target), `apps/farcaster-mobile`, `apps/farcaster-ssr`, plus shared packages (`farcaster-client-hooks`, `farcaster-client-data`, `farcaster-cryptography*`). pnpm 10.8.1, Node 20.19.5, turbo.
- **Node target**: Snapchain read node (`read_node = true`) via `snapchain-bootstrap.sh` in Docker. Default cloud path: AWS EC2 per official guide (~$100/mo); the provision script must be provider-pluggable so any VPS works (LC gateway VPS is the dogfood target).
- **Three-command contract**:
  - (0) `fiddy provision` — script provisions compute (cloud-init / user-data carrying Docker).
  - (1) `fiddy node up` — installs Docker + Snapchain read node, waits for sync health, prints the node's HTTP/gRPC endpoints.
  - (2) `fiddy client up` — boots the client configured with `SNAPCHAIN_HTTP_URL` pointing at the user's node.
  - These wrap the official bootstrap; we do not reimplement Snapchain.
- **Writes**: client submits to its own read node's `POST /v1/submitMessage`; the tutorial teaches the gossip path, the lack of read-node mempool, and `MERGE_MESSAGE`/query-back confirmation. Under load the client offers "submit to a validator endpoint" as a fallback toggle, with the trade-off explained.
- **App keys**: gasless signers only — `makeKeyAddBody`/`makeKeyAdd` + `getGaslessSignedKeyRequestMetadata` from `@farcaster/hub-nodejs` (pin a version that exports them; the upstream PR notes some published versions lack them). Never the onchain key gateway for new keys. Scopes minimal (casts, reactions, links, user data); per-fid nonce strictly increasing; 1000-key cap noted.
- **Seed phrase import**: BIP-39 import of an existing custody address, with a blocking test-account warning screen. Custody key never leaves the client; it signs exactly two things: the EIP-712 `KEY_ADD` authorization and (optionally) fname transfers. All day-to-day signing is the app key.
- **Client filtering (include/exclude casts from other clients)**: filter on the cast's `client` metadata where available / signer-known-client mapping, as a view-layer preference — never a protocol-level claim.
- **One-click deploy service**: an agent (Hermes, on the LC gateway VPS) that accepts cloud credentials or an SSH target, runs the same provision + node scripts, and reports health back to the client UI. Self-hosted by default; no custody of user keys server-side.
- **Fiddy Agent backend**: Agent37 cloud API (`api.agent37.com/v1/instances`) provisions one dedicated Hermes instance per user. The client talks to the instance over the Hermes gateway API (`/v1` chat + profile multiplexing). Channel connections (iMessage/Discord/Telegram/WhatsApp/email) are initiated from the client UI but completed on the instance side, each behind an explicit owner-approval screen — matching the existing fiddy.fun "with your approval on every channel" promise. The agent's Farcaster identity is its own FID with a gasless app key; the owner can revoke it from the client (same `KEY_REMOVE` surface as the client's own app key). Scheduling maps to the instance's cron system; the client exposes a plain-English scheduler UI that writes cron entries. Agent37 keys live server-side only (pattern from `AGENT37-SETUP.md`: hidden prompt, stdin handoff, mode-0600 `.env.local`, status-only checks).
- **Microsite**: static site in `apps/docs-site` (or `site/`), deployed on the LC VPS (fiddy.fun infra, e.g. `client.fiddy.fun` or `fiddy.fun/client`). Quickstart hero on top; tutorial pages beneath; i18n scaffold with zh as first translation.
- **Design**: Solid Glass skill theme tokens + Awwwards skill bar; Fiddy brand assets from `/Users/lc/legitmate-farcaster` (chartreuse, #161715, mascot). Mobile-first CSS verified with the project's existing Playwright mobile config pattern.
- **fiddy.fun sync**: the microsite and deploy agent live on the existing LC gateway VPS alongside the current Fiddy app; the existing Farcaster manifest work (fiddy.fun domain manifest) is untouched by this spec.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior only: node health/sync endpoints respond; `submitMessage` returns success and the cast is queryable back from the node (the real `MERGE_MESSAGE` confirmation path); gasless `KEY_ADD` is accepted and appears in `GET /v1/signersByFid`; client renders feed from the local node with third-party APIs disabled (offline-Neynar test).
- Seam: the node HTTP/gRPC API is the single highest seam — the client never imports node internals. UI tests sit behind the client-data hooks package seam (existing pattern in the monorepo).
- Prior art: the fork's existing package tests and the hello-world example scripts in `farcasterxyz/hub-monorepo`.
- The three commands themselves get an end-to-end smoke script run on a fresh VPS before submission — this is the bounty judge's exact path.
- A human voucher run-through is a launch gate, not an afterthought: recruit early, fix what they trip on.

## Out of Scope

- Running a validator (requires validator-set keys; read node only).
- Onchain account creation / storage purchase flows beyond importing an existing provisioned account (tutorial links out for that).
- Farcaster Mini App / manifest work for fiddy.fun apex (separate pending item).
- Mobile native client polish — web-first; the inherited mobile app stays buildable but is not a bounty deliverable.
- Any custodial handling of user seed phrases server-side. Never.

## Further Notes

- Bounty corrections already incorporated: (1) read nodes DO accept writes and gossip them (snapchain PR #1034); (2) app keys are gasless `KEY_ADD` since mainnet V16 (PR #989) — no Optimism transaction; (3) seed-phrase hygiene is a first-class tutorial section, Unix-`rm` style: powerful, dangerous, test-account-only.
- Known upstream doc gaps worth PR-ing if confirmed while building: the `hello-world` example repo still registers signers onchain; no HTTP API reference page for `/v1/signer` or `/v1/signersByFid`; the step-3/5 snippet variable mismatch (`signer` vs `signerPrivateKey`) flagged by Copilot on PR #989.
- Extra-mile items ranked by signal: more human vouches > Chinese translation > 59s vertical video > anything else.
- Prize: $2,048 / $512 / $128 honorable mentions, USDC to the public Farcaster wallet. Entry = reply cast with microsite URL + repo URL + voucher endorsement URL, within 7 days of the bounty post.

## Summary

**Target Repository:** [`paraloom-labs/paraloom-wallet`](https://github.com/paraloom-labs/paraloom-wallet)
**Severity:** Medium ($150 USDC — Stage 1 Public Beta Bug Bounty)
**Affected Components:**
- `lib/paraloom/swapOutputs.ts` (`saveSwapOutput`, `dismissSwapOutput`)
- `lib/paraloom/privateSwap.ts` (`privateSwap`, `privateSwapFromToken`)
- `lib/paraloom/swapReconcile.ts` (`reconcileSwapOutputs`)
- `lib/paraloom/reshieldRecovery.ts` (`recoverReshields`)
- `lib/storage/secure.ts` (`saveEncryptedWallet`, `migrateWalletToScrypt`, `clearWallet`, `setLockState`, `setAutoLockMinutes`, `updateAccounts`, `setNetwork`)
- `src/background/index.ts` (`maybeAutoLock`, `RESUME_SWAPS`, `handlePrivateSwap`)
- `lib/paraloom/bridge.ts` (`retryingFetch`)
- `lib/paraloom/prices.ts` (`fetchPrices`)

We identified **four distinct concurrency, state-loss, RPC-resilience, and data-validation bugs** in `paraloom-wallet`:

---

## Vulnerability Details

### 1. Unsynchronized Read-Modify-Write Race & Stale-Snapshot Field Clobbering on `paraloom_swap_outputs`, Plus Cross-Context Double Execution of `reconcileSwapOutputs` and `recoverReshields` (`lib/paraloom/swapOutputs.ts`, `lib/paraloom/privateSwap.ts`, `lib/paraloom/swapReconcile.ts`, `lib/paraloom/reshieldRecovery.ts`)

1. **Lost Ephemeral Swap Secret Keys via Unsynchronized `saveSwapOutput` / `dismissSwapOutput` (`lib/paraloom/swapOutputs.ts:34-54`):**
   - `saveSwapOutput` and `dismissSwapOutput` perform unsynchronized `chrome.storage.local.get("paraloom_swap_outputs")` followed by `chrome.storage.local.set(...)` without a Web Lock or queue.
   - In `handlePrivateSwap` (`src/background/index.ts:880-881`), the background worker intentionally launches `void reconcileSwapOutputs(connection, shieldedAddress)` and `void recoverReshields(connection, shieldedAddress)` in the background *without awaiting them*, and immediately starts `privateSwap(...)` / `privateSwapFromToken(...)`. Meanwhile, the popup (`Home.tsx:266-267`) also invokes `reconcileSwapOutputs` and `recoverReshields` on balance refresh.
   - Because `reconcileSwapOutputs` and `recoverReshields` perform slow RPC scans before calling `saveSwapOutput`, a background recovery or popup dismissal that read `paraloom_swap_outputs` before `privateSwap` pre-saved its newly generated `freshAddress` and `freshSecretKeyHex` can finish its `chrome.storage.local.set` *after* `privateSwap`'s pre-save (`privateSwap.ts:323, 526`), overwriting the entire `paraloom_swap_outputs` array with a stale snapshot and **permanently erasing `freshSecretKeyHex` while `spendV3` is withdrawing shielded funds to `freshAddress`**.
2. **Stale-Snapshot Field Clobbering & Dropped `reshield` Flag (`lib/paraloom/swapOutputs.ts:38`, `lib/paraloom/privateSwap.ts:388, 594`):**
   - `saveSwapOutput` merges existing entries via `current[i] = { ...current[i], ...output }`. If a stale caller writes an older `SwapOutput` snapshot with `swapSignature: ""`, `outAmount: 0`, or omitted `reshield` / `reshieldRecovered`, it overwrites an already-recorded `swapSignature`, positive `outAmount`, or `reshieldRecovered: true` flag.
   - Furthermore, the post-submit `saveSwapOutput` calls in `privateSwap` (`lib/paraloom/privateSwap.ts:388`) and `privateSwapFromToken` (`lib/paraloom/privateSwap.ts:594`) omit `reshield: params.reshield ?? false`, risking loss of the `reshield` intent if the pre-save entry was racing.
3. **Cross-Context Double Execution of `reconcileSwapOutputs` and `recoverReshields` (`lib/paraloom/swapReconcile.ts:33`, `lib/paraloom/reshieldRecovery.ts:51`):**
   - `reconcileSwapOutputs` only guards concurrency with a module-local `let reconcileInFlight = false`, which is not shared between the extension popup and the MV3 background service worker; `recoverReshields` has **no concurrency guard at all** (even within the same context when `RESUME_SWAPS` and `handlePrivateSwap` overlap).
   - When popup `loadBalances()` and background `RESUME_SWAPS` / `handlePrivateSwap` run concurrently, both contexts simultaneously classify the same stranded `freshAddress` and invoke `resumeSwapAtFreshAddress` (broadcasting duplicate swap transactions) or Case B `depositSpl` in `recoverReshields` (broadcasting duplicate SPL re-shield transactions).

---

### 2. Unsynchronized `paraloom_wallet` Storage Mutations & Stale-Activity `maybeAutoLock` TOCTOU Race (`lib/storage/secure.ts`, `src/background/index.ts`)

1. **Unsynchronized Read-Modify-Write on `chrome.storage.local["paraloom_wallet"]` (`lib/storage/secure.ts:57-196`):**
   - `saveEncryptedWallet`, `migrateWalletToScrypt`, `clearWallet`, `setLockState`, `setAutoLockMinutes`, `updateAccounts`, and `setNetwork` all read and overwrite the single top-level `paraloom_wallet` object in `chrome.storage.local` without synchronization across popup and background contexts.
   - During legacy vault unlock (`Unlock.tsx`), `migrateWalletToScrypt` and `setLockState(false)` or background `maybeAutoLock` / popup `updateAccounts` / `setNetwork` can interleave their `get` and `set` calls, causing one mutation to overwrite another (reverting `locked: true`, dropping newly added `accounts`, or losing `kdfVersion: 1` / `network` / `autoLockMinutes`).
2. **Stale-Activity TOCTOU Race in `maybeAutoLock` (`src/background/index.ts:61-77`):**
   - `maybeAutoLock()` reads `const last = await getLastActivity()`, then yields across `const autoLockMinutes = await getAutoLockMinutes()`, and then unconditionally calls `await setLockState(true)` and `await clearSession()`.
   - If the user unlocks the wallet (`saveSession` -> `recordActivity()`) or triggers an active operation while `maybeAutoLock()` is suspended at `await getAutoLockMinutes()`, `maybeAutoLock()` resumes with its stale `last` timestamp and immediately wipes the newly created session (`clearSession()`) and locks the wallet (`setLockState(true)`).

---

### 3. `retryingFetch` Fails to Retry HTTP `429` / `408` Rate Limits, and Background Swap/Recovery Connections Omit `retryingFetch` (`lib/paraloom/bridge.ts`, `src/background/index.ts`)

1. **Unretried HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` and `408 Request Timeout` (`lib/paraloom/bridge.ts:36-57`):**
   - `retryingFetch` checks `if (res.status < 500) return res`, immediately returning HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` and `408 Request Timeout` responses without retrying.
   - Because `fetchV3Leaves` issues up to `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1000` sequential `getTransaction` RPC calls and `reconcileSwapOutputs` / `recoverReshields` scan token accounts and transaction histories per swap output, public Solana RPCs frequently return `429 Too Many Requests`, immediately aborting leaf tree reconstruction or swap execution.
2. **Missing `retryingFetch` on Background Swap & Recovery `Connection` Instances (`src/background/index.ts:436, 872`):**
   - While `getConnection()` in `lib/paraloom/bridge.ts` attaches `fetch: retryingFetch`, `src/background/index.ts` constructs bare `new Connection(PRIVATE_SWAP_RPC_URL, "confirmed")` without `fetch: retryingFetch` in both `RESUME_SWAPS` (`line 436`) and `handlePrivateSwap` (`line 872`), leaving all background private swap and recovery RPC calls unprotected against transient `5xx`/`429`/`408`/network errors.

---

### 4. Unvalidated Non-Finite (`NaN`/`Infinity`) and Negative Prices + Unencoded Query Parameters in `fetchPrices` (`lib/paraloom/prices.ts`)

- In `lib/paraloom/prices.ts:34-41`, `fetchPrices` checks `if (v && typeof v.usdPrice === "number")` and `typeof v.priceChange24h === "number"`. In JavaScript, `typeof NaN === "number"` and `typeof Infinity === "number"` are both `true`, and negative `usdPrice` values are not rejected.
- If a malformed or upstream price entry contains a non-finite or negative number, `Home.tsx:792-800` multiplies token balances by `usdPrice` and sums them into `total`, poisoning the entire portfolio USD header into `$NaN`. Additionally, `ids.join(",")` is interpolated into the URL without `encodeURIComponent`, and `clearTimeout(t)` is skipped if `fetch` or `res.json()` throws before line 27.

---

## Fix Summary

1. **`lib/paraloom/swapOutputs.ts` & `lib/paraloom/privateSwap.ts`:**
   - Serialize `saveSwapOutput` and `dismissSwapOutput` under an origin-wide exclusive Web Lock (`paraloom_swap_outputs:write`) with an in-process promise queue fallback.
   - Perform non-destructive field merging in `saveSwapOutput` so a delayed/stale write cannot erase an already-recorded `freshSecretKeyHex`, `swapSignature`, positive `outAmount`, `reshield: true`, or `reshieldRecovered: true`.
   - Include `reshield: params.reshield ?? false` in both post-submit `saveSwapOutput` calls in `privateSwap.ts`.
2. **`lib/paraloom/swapReconcile.ts` & `lib/paraloom/reshieldRecovery.ts`:**
   - Coordinate `reconcileSwapOutputs` (`paraloom_swap_reconcile`) and `recoverReshields` (`paraloom_reshield_recovery`) across popup and background contexts using non-blocking Web Locks (`{ mode: "exclusive", ifAvailable: true }`) alongside in-process guards, and re-verify the latest row state in `listSwapOutputs()` immediately before calling `resumeSwapAtFreshAddress` or `depositSpl`.
3. **`lib/storage/secure.ts` & `src/background/index.ts`:**
   - Serialize all `paraloom_wallet` mutations (`saveEncryptedWallet`, `migrateWalletToScrypt`, `clearWallet`, `setLockState`, `setAutoLockMinutes`, `updateAccounts`, `setNetwork`) under an exclusive Web Lock (`paraloom_wallet:write`) with an in-process queue fallback.
   - Re-check `swapInFlight()` and the latest `getLastActivity()` timestamp in `maybeAutoLock()` before calling `setLockState(true)` and `clearSession()`.
4. **`lib/paraloom/bridge.ts`, `src/background/index.ts`, & `lib/paraloom/prices.ts`:**
   - Export `retryingFetch`, retry HTTP `429` (honoring `Retry-After` up to 5s) and `408` in addition to `5xx`/network errors, and use `getPrivateSwapConnection()` (with `fetch: retryingFetch`) in `RESUME_SWAPS` and `handlePrivateSwap`.
   - Require `Number.isFinite(v.usdPrice) && v.usdPrice >= 0` and finite `priceChange24h` in `fetchPrices`, URL-encode mint IDs with `encodeURIComponent`, and clear the abort timer in `finally`.

items.body:
From the PR #35 security verdict (PASS, minor). ADR-011 promises the `p:` owner link is never seen by the agent, but self-signup lets the agent supply `owner_email`. An agent that gives an inbox it can read receives the owner link and can raise its own limits to the form maximums ($100 bounty, $1000/day).

After signup the isolation holds (link sent once, replies to eyes@ ignored), so this is about who the 'owner' is, not a leak.

Proposed follow-up ADR: also deliver the owner link to the Stripe Checkout payer's email on the first top-up (the person who pays is the owner), and show the masked owner email on the top-up page so a human can see where control went. Related: the public signup can relay one owner email with an 80-char agent name to any address (throttled to 5/hour/IP by T4.1); consider dropping the agent name from that email.
